headline: Occupancy gains lift NOI and earnings; leverage stays flat
summary_short: Cousins Properties' Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 11.8% y/y to $269M on higher occupancy and NOI, and net income available to common stockholders rose 80.6% y/y to $26M, while EBITDA grew 15.6% y/y to $178M even as interest expense rose 22.2% y/y on new bond issuance.
summary_long: NOI rose 9.3% q/q as occupancy gains at Promenade Tower, Avalon, 3350 Peachtree, and Corporate Center lifted same-property income, while the 300 South Tryon and The Link acquisitions drove non-same-property growth; Dallas and Charlotte NOI each rose over 20% y/y. Interest expense rose 22.2% y/y on the February 2026 $500M senior notes issuance, partly offset by a $150M term loan repayment. G&A rose 24.4% y/y on leasing-services compensation tied to the Proscenium joint venture. Long-term debt rose 7.3% y/y to $3,732M; equity fell 6.2% y/y to $4,484M after $90M of Q1 2026 buybacks and steady $0.32/share quarterly dividends. No forward guidance was issued in the filing. Cash remains thin at $6.7M.

drivers.explanation: Occupancy gains at Promenade Tower, Avalon, 3350 Peachtree and Corporate Center plus the 300 South Tryon and The Link acquisitions drove same- and non-same-property NOI growth.
Non-same-property operating expenses rose primarily from the 300 South Tryon (Feb 2026) and The Link (Jul 2025) acquisitions, partly offset by the Harborview and Research Park V dispositions.
Includes a $9.2M gain on the June 2026 sale of Research Park V; six-month net income was also reduced by a $36.6M impairment on One Eleven Congress, sold subsequent to quarter end.
Rose primarily from the February 2026 $500M senior notes issuance and higher credit-facility borrowings, partially offset by a $150M term loan repayment.
Reduced by $90M of Q1 2026 share repurchases and $108M of H1 common dividends ($0.32/share quarterly), only partly offset by net income.
Cash stayed thin as $359.4M of investing outflows, led by the 300 South Tryon acquisition, outpaced $163.4M of net financing inflows and $197.0M of operating cash flow.
Leasing volume stayed strong (924,000 sq ft leased in Q2, new/expansion rent per square foot +26.8%) while the credit facility was upsized to $1.2B and repriced tighter.
